summary: Twin Knobs tower in Mark Twain National Forest, Missouri: site acquired 1936, NHLR-registered 2014, locked and not open to the public.

staffing.status: staffed in fire season by Missouri Department of Conservation (2015 plan)

access.note: Locked behind a tall chain link fence; the 2015 plan says the site is not open for public use

events.note: A December 1936 Howell County Gazette item credits completion to the Willow Springs camp; a former CCC enrollee recalled it under construction in 1935 at the Cabool camp; the 2015 plan says work may have begun before 1936
Forest Service acquired the tower site on April 13, 1936
2015 area plan: determined eligible for listing on the National Register of Historic Places

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The December 1936 newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts credits completion to the Willow Springs camp. The 2015 plan quotes a former CCC enrollee who saw it under construction in 1935 while at the Cabool camp, and says construction may have begun before 1936. The story reports both accounts and does not pick one start date.

sources.title: Douglas & Wright County Towersites Area Management Plan (2015)

notes_for_editor: No height, design or fire history found in the readable sources. The NHLR detail page gives only elevation (1,387 ft, 423 m). The News-Leader article returned HTTP 403, so it was not read. Forest Lookouts is a hobbyist site that quotes a 1936 Gazette item. The MDC plan dates from 2015, so current staffing and fence status are not verified. The removal of the dwelling buildings is a range (late 1960s or early 1970s), so no event year is recorded for it. Site directions in the plan were left out because the site is closed to the public. Brief's 'standing' and 'access unknown' were checked: standing per NHLR; access is closed per NHLR and the 2015 plan. Check 2026-10-09: all 18 quotes were found on the first run; three footnoted claims were corrected (a missing footnote on the dwelling sentence, the 1935 'seeing it' detail, and the undated 'Today' access claim, now dated to the 2015 plan and the NHLR's undated 'currently').
